story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. GitHub Actions workflow file exists at `.github/workflows/daily-rebuild.yml`. Implementation does NOT create a new file — the workflow already exists from Phase 0 Day 2 work (commits 0419fa0, c973c7c, 613a6e8, bef5c10, e46c914). This story formalises the existing workflow against the AC list, closes remaining gaps (AC #6), and verifies it has run on schedule. 2. Workflow triggers daily at 2 AM UTC via cron schedule. Already implemented (lines 9-10: `cron: "0 2 * * *"`). Verification: open the GitHub Actions tab, confirm the workflow appears with a recent scheduled run timestamp matching ~02:00 UTC. Note: GitHub Actions schedules can drift up to 30 minutes during high-load periods — expected and does NOT block AC satisfaction. 3. Workflow includes manual trigger option (`workflow_dispatch`). Already implemented (line 11: `workflow_dispatch:`). Verification: GitHub Actions UI shows a "Run workflow" button; clicking it triggers a manual run that reaches at least the "Build Hugo site" step. 4. Workflow steps cover: Checkout, Setup Node/Hugo, Fetch engagement data (placeholder), Build Hugo, Deploy to GitHub Pages. Already implemented (lines 35-133) with intentional refinements over the Phase 0 task breakdown: `actions/checkout@v4` with `ref: main` + `fetch-depth: 0`; `actions/setup-node@v4` node 22; `peaceiris/actions-hugo@v2` hugo 0.161.1 extended; `sudo snap install dart-sass` (required because of Hugo dartsass transpiler); `npm install`; `node scripts/fetch-umami-hearts.js` + inline `echo '{"children":[]}' > data/webmentions_raw.json` + `node scripts/process-webmentions.js` + `node scripts/calculate-popularity.js`; worktree-based commit to data-updates branch; `actions/configure-pages@v5`; `git describe` → version.txt; `hugo --environment production --minify --baseURL ...`; `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`; `actions/deploy-pages@v4`. Hugo version drift flag: architecture doc says `'0.152.2'`; actual is `'0.161.1'` (intentional, current pinned version). 5. Workflow runs successfully on schedule. Verification step: open GitHub Actions tab → "Daily Rebuild with Engagement Data" → confirm at least ONE successful scheduled run exists with `cron`-triggered status (not `workflow_dispatch`-triggered) AND `conclusion: success`. If no scheduled run exists yet, wait one cycle and verify on the next day. If scheduled runs are failing while manual runs succeed, investigate (typical causes: secrets not loaded for scheduled runs, branch protection rules, GitHub Actions billing limits) and fix before marking done. 6. Build failures send email notification to repository owner. NOT IMPLEMENTED in current workflow file — the primary gap this story closes. Two-layer approach: Layer 1 (built-in, zero workflow change) — GitHub auto-emails the repo owner on workflow failures iff the user has enabled "Actions → Failed workflows only" in their personal Notifications settings. Verify enabled. Layer 2 (explicit, workflow-enforced) — add a final step `if: failure()` that uses `actions/github-script@v7` to call `github.rest.issues.create()` summarising the failure (steps that ran, link to the failed run, timestamp). Issue creation triggers GitHub's standard issue-notification email path. Permissions impact: add `issues: write` to the top-level `permissions` block. Label dependency: pre-create `ci-failure` and `automated` labels OR omit `labels: [...]` from the script. 7. Workflow sets proper Git user for commits. Already implemented (line 87-88: `git config user.name "GitHub Actions Bot"` / `user.email "actions@github.com"`). Used by the worktree-based commit to `data-updates` branch. Verification: `git log origin/data-updates --format="%an <%ae>" -1` shows `GitHub Actions Bot <actions@github.com>`. 8. No regression to existing workflow behaviour after AC #6 is added (testability guard). Diff the workflow file before/after — only the new permission line (`issues: write`) and the new "Notify on failure" step block should appear; all existing steps remain byte-equivalent. Trigger a manual `workflow_dispatch` run after the change and confirm it still completes successfully (the `if: failure()` step is skipped on success). Force-test the failure path by introducing a temporary failing step on a feature branch, running the workflow, confirming the issue is created, then reverting. 9. No automated tests added in this story (testability guard). The workflow file is itself a test artifact — a successful run IS the test. At drafting time, `tests/build/` and `tests/e2e/` infrastructure does NOT exist (Story 1.1 status: ready-for-dev, not landed). If those infrastructures land before this story implements, an OPTIONAL build-test assertion validating the workflow YAML syntax (`actionlint` or `yamllint`) could be added — total ~10 lines of CI config. Skip if test infra absent.

doc.section: Story 2.6: Daily Rebuild GitHub Actions Workflow (lines 358-388)
doc.snippet: FR-034 coverage. ACs 1-7 verbatim source. GitHub Issue #67 ("Merge and Deploy") umbrella. Prerequisites: Phase 0 (GitHub Pages configured, secrets added). Dependencies: Epic 3 (engagement fetch scripts added later) — soft dependency. Implementation Note: AC4 "Fetch engagement data" originally proposed as inline `echo` placeholder; actual implementation uses Phase-0 placeholder scripts. Effort: 1 day.

doc.title: PRD - Functional Requirements
doc.snippet: "Site automatically rebuilds daily with fresh engagement data. Rationale: Popularity scores and content sorting stay current. Priority: MVP (Phase 1A - Week 1-2). Validation: GitHub Actions workflow runs daily at 2 AM UTC, site deploys successfully." FR-035-037 cover engagement data fetching, score updates, and history preservation (Epic 3 dependencies that consume this workflow).

doc.title: PRD - Architecture Notes
doc.snippet: Older canonical workflow YAML spec. Superseded by digital-garden-integration-architecture.md lines 470-549 for current canonical form. Both spec exactly `cron: "0 2 * * *"`.

doc.title: Digital Garden Integration Architecture
doc.snippet: "Single GitHub Actions workflow (fetch → process → build → deploy). Atomic operation, simpler debugging, daily cron at 2 AM UTC." Affects Epic 2, 3, 4. Data Architecture decision: separate `data-updates` branch for automated commits — clean main branch, preserves data history.

doc.title: Digital Garden Integration Architecture
doc.snippet: Reference YAML for the workflow. Pre-Phase-0 design used `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3` for deployment; actual current implementation migrated to the modern `actions/configure-pages@v5` → `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` → `actions/deploy-pages@v4` chain. Environment variables `UMAMI_API_KEY`, `UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` consumed by data-fetch step.

doc.title: Digital Garden Integration Architecture
doc.snippet: Hugo build errors: workflow fails immediately (default behavior), no partial builds deployed, error logs in GitHub Actions. API fetch errors: scripts use try/catch and `process.exit(1)` to fail the workflow. This story's AC #6 layered approach (issue + email) builds on the fail-fast pattern.

doc.title: Digital Garden Integration Architecture
doc.snippet: Rule #3: NEVER commit data/*.json files to main branch (only data-updates branch). APPLIES — workflow correctly uses worktree pattern. Rule #7: ALWAYS pin Hugo version in GitHub Actions (rule text says `'0.152.2'` — STALE; actual workflow pins `'0.161.1'`). Architecture-doc cleanup logged for docs/todo.md.

doc.title: Project Architecture (Top-level)
doc.snippet: "Privacy: No data sent to third parties." Informs the AC #6 implementation choice — prefer GitHub-native issue creation (no SMTP marketplace action, no third-party email service) over external email providers, even when AC text says "send email notification".

story-context.constraints: - **NEVER commit data/*.json files to main branch** (Critical Agent Rule #3). Workflow uses worktree pattern at lines 85-98 to commit only to data-updates. Verify the AC #6 patch does not accidentally introduce a `git add data/` to the main branch path. - **ALWAYS pin Hugo version in GitHub Actions** (Critical Agent Rule #7). Current pin `'0.161.1'` is correct. Architecture doc text saying `'0.152.2'` is stale; do NOT downgrade. Logged for docs/todo.md cleanup. - **No template, partial, asset, config, content, or layout changes.** This is a CI/CD-only story. Any such change during implementation is a scope-creep signal — pause and re-read the AC. - **No new npm dependencies for the workflow itself.** `actions/github-script@v7` is built-in; no `package.json` change. - **No new GitHub Secrets required.** AC #6 layered approach uses GitHub's automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the issue-creation API call. No SMTP creds, no API keys. - **Permission expansion** (`permissions: issues: write`) is a CI-config change, not a runtime auth change for the deployed site. - **No automated tests added in this story.** Test infrastructure (`tests/build/`, `tests/e2e/`) does NOT exist yet at drafting time (Story 1.1 status: ready-for-dev). Workflow YAML is itself the test artifact (a successful run IS the test). - **Atomic single-job design.** Workflow is fetch + process + build + deploy in one job (architecture decision lines 28-32). Do NOT split into multiple jobs — partial failures must NOT deploy stale data. - **AC #6 implementation choice: GitHub Issues, not SMTP marketplace action.** Justification: first-party (no security review for fresh marketplace action), no SMTP secret management, persistent audit trail, gracefully degrades if owner mutes notifications. AC text "send email notification" is satisfied via GitHub's automatic email-on-issue-creation flow. - **Diff-friendliness.** Expected diff: ~4-line addition to `permissions:` (one line) and ~17-line addition for the `Notify on failure` step. Single commit acceptable. Force-test on a feature branch before merging. - **Cron drift tolerance.** GitHub Actions schedules can drift up to 30 minutes during high-load periods. AC #2 verification accepts ~02:00 UTC ± drift; do NOT treat scheduled-vs-clock divergence as a failure. - **Coordination with Epic 3.** Phase 1A Stories 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 will replace each `scripts/*.js` placeholder body with real fetch/process logic. The workflow's `node scripts/<name>.js` invocation pattern is the deferred-integration contract surface — preserved across Epic 3 changes. - **Story 3.4 awareness.** "Data commits to data-updates branch" (Story 3.4, currently `backlog`, scope unclear) concerns the worktree pattern already implemented here. Document existing implementation in completion notes for the eventual Story 3.4 drafter. - **No-regression testability guard (AC #8).** After AC #6 patch lands, existing 12 steps must remain byte-equivalent in the YAML; only the permissions line + Notify-on-failure block are new.
